Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
630 PM EST Sun Nov 15 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 214 PM EST Sunday...

Nighttime temperatures are a few to several degrees milder for 
tonight and tomorrow night in most locations.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 214 PM EST Sunday...

1. After upslope snow showers/flurries at elevations above 1500 
feet or so gradually wind down tonight, a dry period will begin 
areawide. Seasonably cool and cloudy conditions into Monday will 
trend sunny on Tuesday as a warming trend begins.

2. Warm and dry weather will persist through mid to late week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 214 PM EST Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Light snow showers in the Adirondacks, northern 
Greens, and northeastern highlands in Vermont have persisted 
into early afternoon. Water vapor imagery shows an additional 
shortwave to our north pivoting towards northeastern Vermont 
which should keep slightly higher chances of showers in this 
region into the evening. To the west, decreasing radar returns 
nearer to KTYX show cloud tops have warmed/lowered, and there 
are some increasing breaks in the clouds cover per webcams and 
satellite imagery. Overall, this suggests further upslope 
precipitation will trend lighter and more intermittent; expect 
no travel impacts given these precipitation rates and 
increasingly localized precipitation. Also, while wet roads 
often leads to risk of ice formation at night, persistent 
northwest flow and cloud layer will prevent radiative cooling 
that is needed for more substantial surface temperature falls. 
In fact, based on recent temperature verification and this 
cloudy and breezy pattern, we went closer to raw model guidance 
and away from bias-corrected and more climatological overnight 
temperatures. As such, think most lower elevation spots will see
low temperatures only bottom out near or slightly above 
freezing rather than well below freezing.

While increasingly anti-cyclonic flow will lead to dry weather 
on Monday, low level moisture will be trapped due to strong 
subsidence. As a result, persistent cloud cover just about
areawide will be likely through the day as winds remain out of 
the northwest. This cloudiness will limit mixing depth and 
heating, so it will be one more day with seasonably chilly 
daytime temperatures in the upper 30s to mid 40s despite rising 
temperatures aloft. In contrast, on Tuesday as the center of a 
large ridge of high pressure to our southwest migrates nearer 
and low level flow becomes southwesterly, we should scatter the 
shallow cloud cover with a mainly sunny sky for most of the day 
anticipated. The combination of a moderating air mass and 
sunshine should lead to the first in a series of days with high 
temperatures at least 10 degrees above normal.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A ridge of high pressure will remain entrenched across 
much of the eastern CONUS for the latter half of this week. The 
result will be a continued period of dry weather. A series of 
shortwave troughs/frontal systems will attempt to break down the 
ridge late in the week toward next weekend. However, the ridge looks 
to hold firm, shunting northern stream systems to our north, with 
perhaps a glancing blow along the international border on Friday. 
Models have some consensus in better chances for precipitation later 
next weekend, but there's not much agreement in deterministic or 
ensemble guidance in exactly how things would play out. In addition 
to the dry weather, temperatures will remain above normal, 
particularly during the day when highs in the 50s will be common 
(low to mid 40s is normal for mid November). Lows will be a bit more 
seasonable due to a fairly favorable radiational cooling pattern; 
lows should remain in the 30s to around 40F most nights.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 00Z Tuesday...At this time, ceilings range between about
2000-4000 ft agl. Over the next 15-18 hours, northwest flow with
adequate moisture will likely keep the region enveloped in
stratus trapped near to below summit levels of our mountains.
Ceilings will likely lower over the next 4-8 hours, and then
only gradually improve around 16-18z Monday. Currently thinking
only KSLK will have a window of IFR ceilings, and KEFK is less
likely, but not impossible. Winds will be northwesterly around 5-10
knots, and perhaps try to trend more westerly beyond that 
16-18z time frame. Approaching 00z Tuesday, clouds will begin to
gradually scatter, lingering in the Northeast Kingdom and 
Adirondacks longest.

Outlook...
